claim: Humans cut a plan branch after a large early loss and choose the best path less often when it runs through that loss. Seen in 3 samples of one task: Huys 2012 (N=46; pruning model predicts 91% of choices), Lally 2017 (N=37; 78% correct without a large loss vs 37% with one, d=2.06), Faulkner 2022 (N=61, pruning model wins), plus a 2015 sample (37/37 subjects prune). Same task and overlapping lab lineage.
agent_test: On a planning task with a known best path through an early loss, measure how often the agent drops that path versus a matched path with no loss, at equal tokens.

claim: Pruning persisted when it cost money: specific pruning did not differ between the -140 group (free) and the -100 and -70 groups (costly). Only Huys 2012 varied the cost; later studies used one loss size.
agent_test: Make the early loss cheap to bypass in one arm and costly in another; check whether the agent still drops the branch. If yes, a bad first step must not trigger a prune alone.

claim: Pruning is not just loss aversion. Adding loss weighting to the pruning model gave little (iBIC 2472 to 2466 in Lally; no gain in Huys 2012), and Faulkner found the large gain weighted about 3x the large loss.
agent_test: Not testable directly on an LLM; a warning that 'bad outcome' signals and 'loss weight' are separate levers.

claim: Pruning acts as an effort saver: pruned choices were faster than other errors and more common on harder problems, and the loss/no-loss accuracy gap grew with depth (34%, 40%, 49% at depth 3/4/5 in Lally). Huys 2012 found an early-loss optimal path was taken more often when the tree was shallow.
agent_test: Vary tree depth and check whether the agent prunes more as per-node budget falls; use depth as a cue to spend more verification.

claim: People also split deep plans into subgoal fragments and reuse stored fragments; pruning acts inside fragments. Generic early stopping (gamma_G) was near zero once fragmenting was modelled, so loss-triggered pruning is the robust part.
agent_test: Compare decompose-then-solve (O3) with and without a rule that a fragment stops at a bad intermediate result; equal tokens.

claim: The link to depression is contested. Huys 2012 found specific pruning correlated with sub-clinical BDI (94% of subjects had low BDI). Lally 2017 did not reproduce it; Faulkner 2022 found no difference in unmedicated depressed adults (N=30 vs 31, gamma_S 0.630 vs 0.617, p=0.75, BF10=0.27; BDI r=0.068). The mood link is unsupported.
agent_test: Do not build mood-driven pruning into the agent on this basis.

claim: Pruning is higher in methamphetamine use disorder (N=40 vs 49): aversive pruning 0.33 vs 0.15, F(1,100)=16.46, d=0.81; fewer points (2034 vs 3145); equal accuracy where no large loss. One sample.
agent_test: Shows pruning is measurable (parameter recovery r>=0.91) and costs payoff when overused; model it as a rate that can be too high.

claim: Anxiety link is weak. A breathing-resistance anxiety induction did not raise pruning (main effects ps>=0.058; Group x Resistance p=0.025 with users pruning slightly less), and state anxiety related to the loss/no-loss accuracy gap in Lally only at p=0.042 uncorrected.
agent_test: Prompt-induced anxiety (c19) is the only LLM analogue; test whether anxious framing makes an agent drop branches after a failure.

claim: The subgenual cingulate tracked the trial-by-trial pruning inclination (peak t(36)=3.87, pSVC=0.004), a small-volume corrected effect from one fMRI sample.
agent_test: No agent test; do not rely on the neural localisation.

claim: Formal models agree that a fixed bias to cut branches after aversive outcomes distorts learning: aversive states are under-sampled so their badness is under-estimated (Dayan and Huys 2008), and a fixed avoidance bias blocks discovery of a large reward behind pain (Mahajan 2025). A bias gated by outcome uncertainty keeps safety and loses less efficiency. Both are simulations; Mahajan adds a small human VR test (N=28).
agent_test: Allow a prune only while evidence is certain; re-open a pruned branch when a check shows the cut rested on an uncertain signal. Compare fixed vs gated pruning at equal tokens.

claim: Rational-use models say search depth should shrink under time pressure and stop when expected gain falls below cost (Sezener 2019: 2000 ms vs 700 ms groups; Keramati 2011). Some pruning is rational, not only a bias. Callaway 2022 was not read.
agent_test: Tie search depth to a token budget by problem difficulty; G12 already does this.

claim: In LLM tree search, pruning on a model-given value score gives large gains over plain chain of thought: Game of 24 GPT-4 CoT 4%, ToT b=1 45%, b=5 74%. But best-of-100 CoT is 49%, so part of the gain is compute. Other tree methods agree: RAP 64% Blocksworld, LATS 92.7 HumanEval, ToolTree about +10%.
agent_test: Compare a tree with value pruning against best-of-N at equal tokens; the honest ToT gap is 74 vs 49, not 74 vs 4.

claim: LLM pruners are imperfect and cut correct branches: ToT crosswords (evaluator called valid rare words impossible; no-prune solved 4/20 games, 3 missed by the pruned run); PAC-CF found top-K=4 removed the reference action on 64.4% of conflict frontiers (full path kept in 0/24). Gap search: on a biased scorer (PAC-CF TSP50 conflict frontiers) the correct step was removed 64.4% of the time at K=4 even with 16 repeats; resampling the scorer did not help.
agent_test: Log every pruned branch; revive pruned siblings when the chosen branch fails a code check (cheap backtrack).

claim: The generator is the bottleneck in tree search, not the judge: GPT-4 generate with GPT-4 judge 74%, with GPT-3.5 judge 64%; GPT-3.5 generate with GPT-4 judge 31%.
agent_test: Spend the stronger model on generating attempts and use code checks or a cheaper judge for pruning.

claim: Self-evaluation is unreliable as a prune trigger without an outside signal: GPT-3.5 kept its answer 74.7% of the time on GSM8K and changed right to wrong more often than wrong to right; oracle labels helped, no-oracle did not. This conflicts with ToT, where self-scored pruning helps on Game of 24 (checkable arithmetic).
agent_test: Prune only on a code-checkable signal (failing output); test self-score pruning against code-signal pruning on the same trees.

claim: The mirror failure is dropping a good line too early: reasoning models switch thoughts (wrong answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more switches; over 70% of wrong responses contain a correct thought). LLM four-in-a-row players search 1.78 plies on average vs 4-6 for humans, and win rate rose with breadth, not depth.
agent_test: Measure how often a correct thought appears and is abandoned; test a rule holding a thought for a minimum number of steps before switching.

claim: Cutting a trace on an internal bad signal saves tokens at small cost: DeepConf online cuts up to 84.7% of tokens (its 99.9% AIME25 accuracy is offline mode, a different setting); ThinkPrune cuts length by about two thirds (R1-1.5B 10,355 to 3,574 tokens) with accuracy slightly up on average; TIP raised QwQ-32B AIME24 from 38.3 to 44.1.
agent_test: Add a confidence-based early stop to the attempt loop and compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: A monitor that prunes invalid actions was the most important module of a brain-inspired LLM planner: removing it raised invalid moves to 31% in Tower of Hanoi. Rule-based legality pruning is exact, unlike loss-triggered pruning.
agent_test: Prune by code-checked legality or constraint violation, never by model opinion.

claim: Novelty pruning of thought nodes works only when tuned: up to 20x token cut at equal performance, but a badly tuned version gave near-zero solves and cost over 100% more.
agent_test: Any new prune rule must be tuned on a dev set and shown to win at equal tokens before use (G7).

claim: Causal test of what a trace uses: removing the chosen move's branch changed the move 32.0% of the time, removing the final decision 2.1%, removing the largest unchosen branch 1.2%. Deep paragraphs added nothing.
agent_test: Delete unchosen branches from a trace and see whether the answer changes; if not, the written tree does no work and can be cut.

claim: No located study tests loss-triggered Pavlovian pruning in an LLM. Nearest evidence is indirect: anxiety prompts raise biased answers (beta=0.08, p=.02; 6 of 12 models passed checks), models are loss averse (Claude highest of three), emotion prompts change accuracy. Gap search (partial, APIs rate-limited) still found none.
agent_test: Run the Huys maze in text form: compare the LLM's optimal-path rate with and without a large early loss on the path, at equal tokens. This is the open experiment.

claim: Schema rule: 'prune after a bad first step' is an effort saver in humans but a known bias there, and unreliable LLM evaluators make it risky. Allow it only as a reversible, logged, code-triggered cut with a revival rule.
agent_test: Arm A no pruning, arm B prune after a failing code check with revival, arm C prune on self-score; same token budget; compare solve rate.

claim: Score-based pruning is not reliably better than plain sampling at equal compute. Beam search with a learned PRM wins on medium-hard items at small budgets, loses its edge at large budgets and hurts on easy items (Snell 2024). A balanced tree search (REBASE) beat sampling with fewer FLOPs on small 2024 models (Wu 2024: 45.0% at 1.36e14 vs 42.8% at 8.70e14 FLOPs, Mistral-7B, MATH500), while MCTS did not. For a 2025 reasoning model, extending one line (s1, Wait) beat parallel voting. No equal-token ToT vs best-of-N test on 2025-26 frontier models was found.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare prune-and-expand against best-of-N and one long line, split by item difficulty; turn pruning on only where it won.

claim: Holding a thought longer before switching helps reasoning models, but only with a mild, bounded hold. A penalty on switch tokens for 600 tokens (alpha=3) raised AIME2024 pass@1 from 38.3 to 44.1 (QwQ-32B) and 61.4 to 64.1 (R1-Distill-32B); a strong penalty with windows over 300 tokens lowered dev accuracy; a prompt-only version did not help DeepSeek-R1 (72.4 vs 73.8). So a bad-first-step cut should wait, and a prompt rule alone may not enforce it.
agent_test: Vary the minimum number of tokens before an agent may abandon a line (0, 300, 600, 1000) on a fixed problem set; find where accuracy peaks.

claim: Mixing a real test result into the abort decision helps over a bare critic: CodeTree HumanEval 94.5 with node-abort evaluation vs 91.5 without; 92.7 with execution output only (GPT-4o-mini). Abort returns the search to sibling nodes, a weak revival. A clean comparison of test-triggered vs self-score pruning at equal tokens, and of an explicit revival rule, was not found.
agent_test: On a code task, prune on failing tests vs on self-score, equal tokens; add a rule that revives the best pruned sibling when all live branches fail.

claim: LLM reasoning trees grow in breadth, not depth, with effort. Across 14 models in four-in-a-row mean max depth was 1.78 plies (human 4-6); breadth predicted wins (beta=0.075, p=0.0025) and depth did not (p=0.82). No LLM test of depth-dependent loss pruning (human gap 34/40/49% at depth 3/4/5) exists.
agent_test: Raise tree depth in the Huys-style task for an LLM and record the loss/no-loss optimal-path gap at each depth.
